title.narrative: Lifesaving and resilience -building WASH and FSL intervention in Dar'a and Deir ez Zor governorates.

description.narrative: ltpgtltbrgtOxfam proposes a 12-month multisectoral humanitarian response in underserved communities of Izra’ and Da’el sub-districts in Dar’a governorate and Deir ez-Zor city in Deir ez-Zor governorate. The project aims to improve access to safe water, sanitation, food, and essential services for 75,280 vulnerable individuals, including returnees, IDPs, and host communities, in alignment with the clusters’ objectives priorities. These areas are among the SHF-prioritized sub-districts with inter-sector severity scores of 4 and are experiencing increased pressure on services due to recent returns and ongoing displacement. Additionally, Oxfam coordinated with relevant sectors, local authorities, and humanitarian actors (including EPDC, TGH, PUI and GVC) to ensure complementarity and avoid duplicationltbrgtThe proposed intervention is informed by Oxfam’s assessments and consultations with local authorities, community representatives, and sectors. In Dar’a, Oxfam will rehabilitate three boreholes (two in Mahjeh and one in Abtaa) with solar systems, and upgrade water networks in Izra’ city to improve water access for 18,500 people. In parallel, Oxfam will address sanitation risks for 20,000 individuals by repairing sewage systems in Izra’ and Dael, mitigating environmental and public health hazards.ltbrgtAdditionally, the project will rehabilitate a bakery in Izra’ town, adding a second production line to increase daily bread output from 8.3 to over 16 tons. This will directly benefit 33,880 people by improving access to affordable bread and reducing food insecurity. The bakery design includes gender-sensitive considerations such as separate queues, as well as considering PWD and elderly-friendly access.ltbrgtIn Deir ez-Zor, Oxfam will scale up its MPCA response, through six rounds of Multi-Purpose Cash Assistance (MPCA), 580 households (2,900 individuals) will receive timely support to meet urgent needs, including food, rent, and essential services. This builds on Oxfam’s ongoing MPCA programming in the area and is designed to reduce reliance on negative coping strategies.ltbrgtThis integrated response aligns with and contributes to Envelopes 1 (80%) and 2 (20%) of the allocation strategy by addressing acute needs (WASH, bread and MPCA) and improving access to basic services (WASH and bread) in the targeted areas, enhancing and setting up the living circumstances to support safe and dignified returns.ltbrgtIt is worth highlighting that the MPCA intervention targets all community categories, combining sector priorities under both envelopes 1 2. The bakery rehabilitation is linked to the FSA priority under envelope 1 “Addressing critical food security gaps and promoting lifesaving agricultural and livelihood support for crisis-affected populations”. The WASH programming is also under the sectoral priority under envelope 1 “Strengthening community capacity and infrastructure to sustain WASH services and mitigate public health risks for IDPs and host communities at risk”.ltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtSectoral activities are geographically and programmatically aligned to maximize impact and avoid duplication.ltbrgtIn Dar’a, WASH infrastructure rehabilitation—including boreholes and sewage systems—is complemented by bakery rehabilitation under FSA, improving both public health and food access. The upgraded water network in Izra’ supports the bakery’s increased production capacity, reinforcing household food security and reducing reliance on negative coping strategies.ltbrgtIn DeZ, MPCA enables vulnerable HHs to meet urgent needs, including food and rent, while indirectly stimulating local markets and enhancing access to WASH services. The cash modality is informed by market assessments and complements ongoing WASH and FSA programming funded by other donors.ltbrgtCross-sectoral coordination is embedded in targeting, community engagement, and monitoring frameworks. Gender and protection considerations are mainstreamed across all sectors, ensuring inclusive access and reinforcing resilience.ltbrgtlt/pgt
